name: Question 11
problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3+2\text{i} \\ 4+\text{i} \\ 2+6\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=4-\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=3,$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{3},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {\lambda }_{3}\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & {v}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{3}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vectors v1 and v3 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where the 2×2 block of B represents a rotation-scaling matrix: v1=[3+2i4+i2+6i],v3=[203],B=[4−10140003] The vectors v1 and v3 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=4−i and λ3=3, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a real 3×3 matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ3 with corresponding eigenvector v3, and two complex eigenvalues λ1=λ―2 with corresponding eigenvectors v1=v―2, then A=PBP−1, where B=[Re(λ1)Im(λ1)0−Im(λ1)Re(λ1)000λ3],P=[|||Re(v1)Im(v1)v3|||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

From our block diagonal matrix B=[4−10140003], we deduce that the first and second columns of P will correspond to the complex eigenvector v1, and the third column of P will correspond to the real eigenvector v3:

P=[322410263]
